henry.title: Autumn Senses Poem
henry.intro: Poets use the 5 senses: see, hear, smell, taste, touch. Today you'll collect real fall sense words and turn them into a 5-line poem. (About 15 minutes.)
steps: FIRST (5 min): Sense hunt! Go outside or to a window, and the kitchen. For each sense, write one fall thing on question 1. Example: see: yellow cottonwood leaves, smell: roasting green chile.
NEXT (7 min): Turn each word into one line of your poem (question 2). Start each line with 'I see', 'I hear', 'I smell', 'I taste', 'I feel'. Example: I hear leaves crunch under my shoes.
LAST (3 min): do questions 3 and 4. You're done when your poem has 5 lines and a title!
worksheet: Sense hunt: see ________ hear ________ smell ________ taste ________ touch ________
Describing words (adjectives) tell what something is like, like crunchy or golden. Underline 2 in your poem.
A simile compares with 'like' or 'as'. Example: The leaves are as red as chile. Write one: ____________________

frankie.title: P is for Pumpkin! 🎃
frankie.intro: Grown-up, read aloud: P says /p/, like pop, pie and pumpkin! (About 10 minutes.)
steps: Grown-up: say 'p-p-pumpkin' and pop your lips together. Frankie copies you.
P hunt (4 min): find 3 things at home that start with /p/ (pillow, pan, pencil, plate, pajamas).
Worksheet: trace the P's, circle the P pictures, draw a pumpkin. Done!
worksheet: Draw one P thing you found at home
links: Bonus with a grown-up: play a Super Why letter game.
